description:
MEASURED s396 at session end (the artifact-staleness check CLAUDE.md asks for
after an emission-changing commit).  Filed rather than fixed, because
regenerating is a real change that needs its own pack.t verification window --
see BAR.

BOTH CHECKED-IN TRANSPILED ARTIFACTS ARE AT gen v2-136; the compiler is at
v2-147.  ELEVEN generations of drift, accumulated across s387-s395 (not s396 --
see NOT MINE below).

  cl/pcl-pack.lisp   body 2958 lines checked in vs 3081 regenerated
                     496 diff lines
  cl/pcl-mro.lisp    18 diff lines

This is the exact failure mode CLAUDE.md's pack.t note warns about: the file
"was found at gen v2-30 against a v2-71 compiler -- 40 generations of drift,
which made every pack.t run a test of the OLD emitter."  Every pack.t and mro
run today is again testing an emitter eleven generations behind.

WHAT THE DRIFT IS (characterized, so the regeneration is not a surprise):
  * +149 `(p-defcell $x ...)` forward declarations the current compiler emits
    and the v2-136 one did not;
  * the COND-RENAME family is gone: the artifact has `(let (($i__cond__0 0)) ...
    (p-incf-raw $i__cond__0))` where the current compiler emits plain `$i` plus
    the p-defcell above it -- i.e. direction D's "a `let` of a symbol-macro name
    SHADOWS it" replaced the rename.  ~24 sites in pack.
  * the rest is layout/nesting of the same forms (p-<, p-+, p-&&, p-int).

NOT MINE (checked, do not re-derive): s396's only emission change is the
`\(EXPR)`-as-lvalue list-context fix, and NEITHER diff contains a single
p-backslash / p-list-= / p-refgen line.  lib/mro.pm has no `\(` at all, and
cl/pack-impl.pl's four are escaped parens INSIDE die-message string literals.
So s396 did not oblige a regeneration; the debt predates it.

BAR (from tools/rebuild-pack's own header, do not shortcut it):
  tools/rebuild-pack
  perl sweep-perl-tests.pl --jobs 1 --timeout 380 perl-tests/pack.t
  tools/sweep-diff.pl          # expect 0 new
then the same for cl/pcl-mro.lisp from lib/mro.pm, then the Pl/t gate and a
full sweep (both artifacts are loaded by the runtime, so corpus-diff cannot see
the change -- the s377 "a lib/ or cl/ change makes the sweep NON-OPTIONAL" rule
applies).

WORTH ADDING WHILE THERE: a staleness CHECK, so this cannot accumulate again
silently -- the artifacts carry their generation in line 1
(`;;; pcl: pipeline=v2 gen=v2-136`), so comparing that against
*pcl-cache-generation* is a two-line test.  A Pl/t row, or a step in
tools/prove-core, would turn eleven generations of silent drift into a failing
row the session it happens.
subject: cl/pcl-pack.lisp + cl/pcl-mro.lisp are ELEVEN generations stale (gen v2-136 vs v2-147) - every pack.t run tests the old emitter
